_comment: Which prose document describes which part of the code, and a content hash of
that code as it was when the document was last read against it.
scripts/doc_reconciliation.py turns this into 'which documents are OWED a
reading' -- the mechanical half of doc rot. Whether a document is TRUE is not
mechanical; conformance/declared_not_implemented.json pins the claims already
last_read = null is honest, not an omission: tracking began 2026-09-19, and a
baseline hash was recorded for every document then, but only the documents
with a last_read entry were actually read against the code that day. The
rest are owed a reading and the report says so on every run.
Adding a document here is the right response to finding a stale claim in
one. 'subjects' are the paths whose change should send someone back to it.
